stories.headline: Drone strikes UAE's Barakah nuclear power plant, triggering fire and raising ceasefire alarm
stories.summary: A drone breached UAE air defences on May 17 and struck an electrical generator outside the inner perimeter of the Barakah Nuclear Energy Plant in Abu Dhabi's Al Dhafra region, causing a fire. Radiological safety levels were unaffected and no injuries were reported; the UAE defence ministry said two other drones were intercepted. The UAE blamed Iran or its proxies, with Foreign Minister Abdullah bin Zayed condemning the strike in calls with the IAEA director-general and Arab counterparts, and invoking the UAE's right to respond to 'terrorist attacks.'

stories.headline: Netanyahu claims secret wartime visit to UAE; Abu Dhabi denies, Israel's security chiefs also said to have visited
stories.summary: Israel's Prime Minister's Office announced that Netanyahu secretly visited the UAE and met President MBZ in Al-Ain on March 26 during 'Operation Roaring Lion,' calling it a 'historic breakthrough.' The UAE Foreign Ministry immediately denied any such visit took place, while multiple Israeli and Arab sources subsequently confirmed the meeting occurred. Reports then emerged that the IDF chief of staff, Mossad director, and Shin Bet chief also made covert visits to Abu Dhabi during the conflict, further exposing deep wartime UAE-Israel intelligence and defence cooperation.

stories.headline: PM Modi's Abu Dhabi stopover yields defence pact, $5B investment, and ADNOC energy deals
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi made a brief two-to-three hour stopover in Abu Dhabi on May 15, meeting President MBZ and signing six to seven agreements spanning a strategic defence framework partnership, strategic petroleum reserve expansion (ADNOC to store up to 30 million barrels in India), LPG supply, a $5 billion UAE investment package in India (including $3B in RBL Bank by Emirates NBD, $1B from ADIA to NIIF), and a G42–C-DAC term sheet for an 8-exaflop AI supercomputer cluster in India. Modi praised MBZ for 'courage and wisdom' in difficult circumstances and condemned Iranian attacks on the UAE.

stories.headline: UAE secretly struck Iran's Lavan Island refinery; tried and failed to rally Gulf states for coordinated military response
stories.summary: Multiple reports, led by The Wall Street Journal, revealed that the UAE covertly conducted airstrikes against Iran's Lavan Island oil refinery in April, knocking out most of its refining capacity. President MBZ also held calls with Saudi Crown Prince MBS and other Gulf leaders arguing for a collective retaliatory response to Iranian missile and drone attacks on the UAE, but Saudi Arabia and Qatar refused, saying it was 'not their war.' The episode highlighted a widening rift between the UAE and its Gulf partners, with the UAE also secretly coordinating intelligence and air defence with Israel during the conflict.

stories.headline: ADNOC ordered to fast-track West-East Pipeline to double Hormuz-bypass export capacity by 2027
stories.summary: Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed directed ADNOC to accelerate construction of the new West-East 1 Pipeline, which will double the UAE's oil export capacity through Fujairah (outside the Strait of Hormuz) from approximately 1.5–1.8 million barrels per day to over 3 million bpd, with operations expected by 2027. The directive came at an ADNOC Board Executive Committee meeting and was widely covered as a direct response to the Strait of Hormuz blockade by Iran. ADNOC Drilling also signalled readiness to push production capacity beyond the 5 million bpd target if asked.

stories.headline: Mubadala Energy takes final investment decision on $13B Commonwealth LNG project in Louisiana
stories.summary: Mubadala Energy and partners Kimmeridge and CPP Investments announced the final investment decision for the Caturus Commonwealth LNG export project in Louisiana, closing $9.75 billion in project financing. Mubadala holds a 24.1% stake in the Caturus platform and is also an equity participant in the financing. The facility targets 9.5 million tonnes per annum capacity and is expected to generate over $3 billion in annual export revenue once operational in 2030.

stories.headline: Mubadala invests $325M in world's largest offshore wind farm, Hornsea 3
stories.summary: Mubadala Investment Company announced a $325 million investment in Ørsted's Hornsea 3 offshore wind project in the UK, joining an Apollo-managed consortium. Once completed, the 2.9GW facility will be the world's single largest offshore wind farm, expected to power more than 3.3 million UK homes. The investment extends Mubadala's growing global renewable energy portfolio.
